text:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency SLO burn detected for inference-prod-us-east-1. p99 = 4.2s (SLO=1s) — automated page dispatched to eng-oncall. metric: inference.latency.p99 > threshold.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: page fired -> escalation policy: eng-oncall-primary. Incident ID: INC-6505012345. Pager: erin.

erin: acked the page, on it. any customer-facing impact reported?

sam: looking at dashboards — spike started ~6505012280, correlated with a burst from batch jobs hitting long-seq paths.

nerin: thanks sam. digging into hotpath tail, checking KV-cache evictions.

naveen: I see repeated batch window at 6505012200..6505012300 causing large KV cache churn on hosts us-east-1-a. eviction rate x5.

cheng: curious if autoscaler kicked? checking autoscale events.

sam: autoscaler did add pods but they cold-started, tokenizer warmup dominates first-second latency. warmup time ~2.8s per replica.

erin: that explains high p99. mitigation: 1) scale-up prewarmed pool 2) enable fallback to smaller quantized model for burst 3) temporarily increase suppression to avoid pagerflood if noisy.

incident-bot: Runbook hint: follow 'latency-tail-burst' runbook. Steps 1..5.

pagerduty-bot: Note: page auto-suppression not active. Current noise filter threshold = 10min window.

naveen: quick commands:
```bash
# live tail of sidecar logs for us-east-1
kubectl logs -n inference -l shard=us-east-1 --tail=200 | grep "kv-evict\|tokenizer"
# check autoscaler events
kubectl get hpa -n infra inference-scaler -o yaml | sed -n '1,120p'
```

cheng: I ran the first cmd — seeing repeated "cache miss -> evict" lines and tokenizer init messages.

erin: on-call decision: trigger emergency warm pool and enable fallback model. sam please run playbook.

sam: running warm-pool play now. ETA ~45s. Also triggering model-fallback via config flag.

pagerduty-bot: erin acknowledged. PagerDuty: is still open.

incident-bot: action recorded: warm-pool initiated by sam at 6505012330. fallback flag toggled by sam at 6505012340.

naveen: after toggling fallback, p99 dropped to 1.1s within ~20s. not back to baseline but much better.

erin: good. can we suppress further autopages for this signal while we observe? I want to avoid duplicate pages for the same root cause (white-noise bursts).

sam: we can flip auto-suppression to 15m for this alert group — I'll do it and leave a note.

cheng: note: suppression helps avoid pagerflood but we should not hide new distinct incidents. set suppression to dedupe by fingerprint (host+eviction-rate) rather than global.

erin: agreed. set dedupe key. sam, can you add that to follow-up?

sam: done — added dedupe by host+evictRate and 15m cooldown. commit link: https://git.internal/alerts/merge/1234

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: manual suppress applied by sam. Suppression expires in 15m.

incident-bot: monitoring: p99 stable at ~1.0-1.2s; p95 normal.

erin: switching to watch mode. handing to oncall-rotation for 1hr postmortem and customer comms assessment. @oncall-rotation please pick up.

oncall-rotation: ack. I'll coordinate post-incident notes and check for any customer API errors to surface.

naveen: quick note: root cause seems to be overlapping batch windows leading to KV cache thrash + cold tokenizer starts. Long term: we should prewarm tokenizer and stagger batch schedules.

erin: action items:
- sam: keep suppression config and post merge diff (done)
- naveen: propose scheduler staggering + warm-pool plan by EOD
- cheng: verify fallback model quality regressions on critical evals (if any)
- oncall-rotation: draft customer impact statement if any users saw >3s responses

sam: I'll start that checklist now.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. No active page expected until suppression expires or metric rises again.

erin: resolving on pagerduty once we confirm stability for 10m.

sam: p99 remains ~1.1s at 6505012380. handing off. :thumbsup:

oncall-rotation: received handoff. will open a retro thread.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: incident state remains acknowledged. Pager will close when user resolves or auto-resolve triggers.

incident-bot: logged incident summary: "KV-cache thrash during batch overlap -> cold tokenizer warmups -> p99 spike". Incident ID INC-6505012345.

erin: thanks team. follow-ups on postmortem channel later.

sam: small tip for the suppression config we used: add a 'white-noise' filter that requires sustained >2x p99 for 3 consecutive windows before paging, prevents single-window spikes from firing. I'll add a draft PR.

cheng: good idea. also add an alert annotation to link to fallback-runbook to speed future mitigations.

oncall-rotation: closing handoff at 6505012380.

erin: closing thread.
